abstract: Evaluates subterranean structural integrity, rock mechanics, and seismic containment barriers
system_message:
You are Geotechnical and structural lead (GEO). The Geotechnical and structural lead (GEO) evaluates subterranean structural integrity, rock mechanics, and seismic containment barriers for emergency archival repository designations.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Subterranean subsidence monitoring（SURV）
information_points.content:
GEO-SURV-K6R：Interferometric satellite radar monitoring indicates an annual subsidence rate of 1 mm/a across the bedrock strata above the candidate cavern at the Old Quarry Limestone Archive.
GEO-SURV-DXE：Interferometric satellite radar monitoring indicates an annual subsidence rate of 4 mm/a across the bedrock strata above the candidate cavern at the Highland Subterranean Vault Facility.
GEO-SURV-E23：Interferometric satellite radar monitoring indicates an annual subsidence rate of 2 mm/a across the bedrock strata above the candidate cavern at the Valley Redoubt Conservation Repository.

information_points.title: Evaluates subterranean structural integrity, rock mechanics, and seismic containment barriers（STRUC）
information_points.content:
GEO-STRUC-IEY：For facility installations in Sichuan, the Old Quarry Limestone Archive does not hold a seismic stability certification for subterranean chamber structural anchors and vault walls, though its primary artifact vault perimeter bulkheads and blast doors achieve a verified passive fire containment rating.
GEO-STRUC-837：For facility installations in Hubei, the Highland Subterranean Vault Facility lacks seismic stability certification for subterranean chamber structural anchors and vault walls, and does not hold a passive fire containment rating for its bulkheads and blast doors.
GEO-STRUC-E0I：For facility installations in Sichuan, the Highland Subterranean Vault Facility holds a valid seismic stability certification for subterranean chamber structural anchors and vault walls, and its primary artifact vault perimeter bulkheads and blast doors achieve a verified passive fire containment rating.
GEO-STRUC-ALW：For facility installations in Sichuan, the Valley Redoubt Conservation Repository holds a valid seismic stability certification for subterranean chamber structural anchors and vault walls, and its primary artifact vault perimeter bulkheads and blast doors satisfy the passive fire containment rating.
